subsections.title: Overview
subsections.summary: What it is and why it matters.

blocks.html: “The cloud” just means someone else's computer. When your photos, documents and backups sync to a cloud service, that company holds a copy — and unless the files are end-to-end encrypted, the company (and anyone who breaks in or sends it a legal request) can read them. Choosing an encrypted provider, or encrypting files yourself before they leave your device, keeps the convenience without handing over the contents.

subsections.title: Terminology
subsections.summary: The words you will run into.

items.title: End-to-end encryption (E2EE)
items.html: Files are encrypted on your device, so the provider only ever stores scrambled data it can’t read.

items.title: Zero-knowledge
items.html: A provider that cannot see your files or password, because only you hold the key.

items.title: Sync vs. backup
items.html: Sync mirrors changes (including deletions) everywhere; a backup keeps older copies you can restore.

items.title: Client-side encryption
items.html: Encrypting files yourself (e.g. with Cryptomator) before uploading them to any service.

items.label: Cryptomator
items.desc: encrypt files before they reach any cloud.
